skill.name: transitions-dev
skill.description: Adds accessible, production-ready CSS transitions for common web interface patterns, with motion tokens, HTML hooks, and focused JavaScript orchestration.
skill.summary: Choose, install, review, and refine 32 reusable web interface transitions.
skill.author: jakubantalik

security_audit.summary: One of 115 static findings is confirmed: the banner stacking example inserts unsanitized HTML and can create XSS when content is untrusted. The other findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, JavaScript template literals, DOM animation reflows, documentation links, and benign interface terminology. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or system command execution was found.

remediation.issue: The banner stacking example inserts contentHTML through innerHTML without sanitization.
remediation.suggestion: Accept plain text and use textContent, build trusted DOM nodes, or sanitize HTML with a maintained library before insertion.

content.user_title: Add Polished CSS Transitions to Web Apps
content.value_statement: Interface motion often becomes inconsistent, inaccessible, or difficult to maintain. This skill provides 32 reusable transition patterns with shared tokens and reduced-motion support.
actual_capabilities: Selects one of 32 documented transition patterns for a specific interface element.
Provides reusable CSS variables for duration, easing, distance, scale, blur, and component motion.
Supplies required HTML hooks and focused JavaScript orchestration for interactive transitions.
Reviews project styles and components for suitable transition patterns without editing files.
Maps existing motion values to documented tokens based on interface usage.
limitations: The patterns require adaptation to each project's markup, selectors, and component state.
Some transitions require JavaScript and careful synchronization with CSS variables.
The skill does not provide visual regression testing or browser automation.
The banner stacking example must not receive unsanitized HTML.

use_cases.title: Animate Product Interfaces
use_cases.description: Add consistent dropdown, modal, tab, tooltip, toast, and form feedback transitions to an application.

use_cases.title: Standardize Motion Tokens
use_cases.description: Replace scattered durations and easing values with a documented motion scale based on interface purpose.

use_cases.title: Review Existing Animations
use_cases.description: Identify interface elements that match the transition catalog and receive file-specific improvement suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Transitions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use transitions reveal to list every available pattern with its purpose and reference file.
prompt_templates.scenario: Explore the catalog before choosing a pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the best transition for this dropdown. Explain the match and identify the required state hooks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Select a pattern for one interface element.

prompt_templates.title: Review Project Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Run transitions review on this project. Group recommendations by file and do not edit anything.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Motion Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Run transitions refine across the project. Map values by interface usage, flag unmatched values, and wait for confirmation before edits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Standardize motion in a mature codebase.

output_examples.input: Suggest a transition for a menu anchored to its trigger.
output_examples.output: Menu dropdown is the best match because the surface opens from an anchor. The response identifies open, close, origin, and accessibility state hooks.

output_examples.input: Review the project for inconsistent animation timing.
output: Recommendations are grouped by source file.
Each item explains the interface purpose and matching motion token.
Values without a documented usage match remain unchanged.

output_examples.input: Add a reduced-motion version of a modal transition.
output_examples.output: The result preserves the modal state model and includes a reduced-motion guard that disables transition effects.

best_practices: Match the visible interface element and user action before selecting a transition.
Preserve every prefers-reduced-motion guard and existing accessibility state.
Keep CSS timing values connected to shared motion tokens.
anti_patterns: Do not replace explicit transitioned properties with transition: all.
Do not duplicate the universal root variables when they are already imported.
Do not pass untrusted HTML into the banner stacking example.

faq.question: How many transitions are included?
faq.answer: The skill documents 32 patterns for common interface states, feedback, navigation, loading, and content changes.

faq.question: Does it require a framework?
faq.answer: No. The CSS is framework independent, and JavaScript examples use browser APIs.

faq.question: Does every transition require JavaScript?
faq.answer: No. Several patterns are CSS only, while stateful or geometry-based patterns include small JavaScript examples.

faq.question: Is reduced motion supported?
faq.answer: Yes. Every pattern includes a prefers-reduced-motion guard that should remain in the final implementation.

faq.question: Can it review an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. The review command identifies matching components and motion values without editing files.

faq.question: Can it safely render dynamic banner content?
faq.answer: Only plain text or trusted, sanitized markup should be used. The provided innerHTML example is unsafe for untrusted content.
